title: Grove's mandate is instrumental: it pursues yield in order to make USDS more attractive, not as an end in itself
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.2 states Grove's Strategic Intent: "Grove will unlock the full potential of **USDS** by building an institutional-grade credit platform designed to facilitate credit creation and seamlessly move yield in and out of the onchain economy. **Grove's priority is to make USDS more attractive** through diversified stability fee streams, more efficient rates, and greater utility, with CLOs as the first step into accessing higher yielding investment-grade credit assets."

The object of the sentence is the stablecoin, not the return. Grove is not chartered to earn yield; it is chartered to make USDS more attractive, and yield is one of three named routes to that — alongside rate efficiency and utility.

This reframes how every Instance in the Artifact should be read. The test for an allocation is not whether it is profitable but whether it strengthens USDS, and the two can diverge. **Diversified** stability fee streams are valuable even where a concentrated portfolio would yield more, because diversification is what makes the fee stream dependable enough to support a peg. A highly profitable allocation that correlates with existing exposures may fail the real test while passing the obvious one.

It also explains the shape of the liquidity layer documented across the rest of the Artifact. Conservative caps, unlimited exit paths, 100% capital charges during burn-in and asset-level exposure ceilings are expensive in return terms and cheap in stability terms — a portfolio optimizing for yield would not look like this. The controls are consistent with the stated objective rather than with the surface activity.

The general point: an Agent whose purpose is instrumental needs its objective written down, because its performance cannot be read off its returns. Without A.6.1.1.2.3.2, Grove's allocations would be assessed against the wrong metric.
